There was a decline of as much as 6% in the number of Indian students in the U.S. for their studies in 2025-26 as compared to the previous year, with just 3,39,435 enrolled in American universities during the year in comparison to 3,63,019 the year before, according to a report by U.S.-based think-tank Institute of International Education (IIE).

According to The Open Doors 2026 Report on International Educational Exchange, most Indian students were studying at the graduate level, with up to 116,609 studying at various universities in 2025-26. This was a 34% decline in comparison to the prior year.
There were also 39,711 Indian students studying at the undergraduate level, one percent lower than the previous year.
Despite the decline, India continues to send the largest chunk of international students to the U.S., the report states.
Indian student enrolments had earlier declined in 2020-21 to 1,67,582 from 1,93,124 in the previous year. After 2020-21, the enrolments continuously rose till 2024-25 and peaked at 3,63,019 before coming down in 2025-26.
The report states that the decline in 2025-26 was due to multiple contributing factors, with 88% of universities citing the visa application process.
In addition, 70% of universities cited travel restrictions, while 60% said students were enrolling in other countries for higher education. Forty-five per cent said that cost was a key factor reducing Indian students’ ability to study in the U.S.
The majority of Indian students go to universities in Texas, New York, Massachusetts, California and Illinois, according to the report.
The number of international students from China decreased by four per cent to 254,458 in 2025-26 as compared to 2,65,919 in the previous year.
Most Chinese students studied at the graduate level — up to 114,043 students — which was a decline of five percent in comparison to the previous year. The number of Chinese students at the undergraduate level also saw a decline of five per cent and stood at 74,594.
The report states that international graduate students were the largest among the different student groups studying at various levels in the U.S., numbering 423,078.
Among graduate students, a decline of 13% was primarily driven by a decline in students pursuing master’s degrees, up to 22%, the report states.
In contrast, doctoral student totals increased by 3% and undergraduate enrolments remained stable at 356,165 students, with a modest 0.3% decline.
“The number of new international students, those at their college or university for the first time, decreased by 18% to 228,123,” the report states.
Overall, the number of international students in the US declined 2.7% from 11,77,766 in 2024-25 to 11,46,163 in 2025-26, according to the report.
Most international students (57%) studied in the STEM fields, with math and computer science (286,168) and engineering (214,193) as the top fields.
International students accounted for 6% of the total U.S. higher education population, and most of these students were hosted by public institutions (59%).
International students contributed nearly $56 billion to the U.S. economy in 2025, according to the U.S. Department of Commerce, the report states.
